readme_key_control_run.purpose: The brief only required the `readme` key. I probed whether declaring it explicitly buys anything over cargo's auto-detection of a package-root README.md — i.e. whether the key is load-bearing or decorative.
readme_key_control_run.output: error: readme `READ-ME-NOT-THERE.md` does not appear to exist (relative to .../fathomdb-query). Please update the readme setting in the manifest at .../Cargo.toml
readme_key_control_run.reading: The explicit key IS load-bearing: it converts 'README silently missing from the crates.io page' (the 0.8.9 state on all 7 crates, which auto-detection produced without a murmur) into a LOCAL hard failure. A rename or a move now fails on the machine. This is the one piece of registry metadata in this leg that cargo really does validate locally.

brief_and_design_citations_found_to_be_w.severity: MATERIAL — it is the stated premise of HITL seq-198
brief_and_design_citations_found_to_be_w.claim: Brief Task C: 'They are validated LOCALLY by `cargo package`, so a mistake fails before anything leaves the machine — which is exactly why keywords are in scope and `categories` is not.' The design of record §4 says the same thing ('validated locally by `cargo package`, so a mistake fails before anything leaves the machine').
brief_and_design_citations_found_to_be_w.finding: FALSE for cargo 1.95.0. `cargo package` performs NO keyword validation whatsoever. Three deliberate controls on fathomdb-query, each run as a real `cargo package --no-verify --allow-dirty` (not just --list):
controls: 6 keywords (limit is 5)                     -> rc=0, 'Packaged 8 files'. Also rc=0 under `cargo package --list`.
a keyword with a space and a '!' (illegal)  -> rc=0, 'Packaged 8 files'
brief_and_design_citations_found_to_be_w.restore: git checkout -- src/rust/crates/fathomdb-query/Cargo.toml after each; final `git status --porcelain` on that path empty.
brief_and_design_citations_found_to_be_w.consequence: Keywords are validated SERVER-SIDE by crates.io at publish, in the same place and at the same moment as categories. The seq-198 distinction between them therefore does NOT hold on the axis the ruling names. It survives on a DIFFERENT axis, and only that one: keyword rules are simple, closed and mechanically checkable offline (<=5, <=20 chars, [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*), whereas a category must match an opaque server-side taxonomy that cannot be checked without the registry. So the residual risk here is much lower than for categories — but it is not zero for the reason given, and nothing in this repo currently checks it. A bad keyword on tier T5 would wedge the publish AFTER T1-T4 uploaded immutably: precisely the v0.8.9 partial-publish shape.
brief_and_design_citations_found_to_be_w.what_I_did_about_it: I did NOT rely on cargo. I wrote and ran an independent tomllib+regex check over all 7 committed manifests asserting count/length/charset/first-char, plus readme and categories-absence. All 7 clean. Evidence under keywords_per_crate.independent_mechanical_validation.
brief_and_design_citations_found_to_be_w.HAND_OFF: Slice 40 (R-20-PUB) should add this ~15-line assertion to the release preflight — the natural home is `scripts/verify-release-gates.sh` beside check 5, which already walks every publishable manifest for description/license/repository. I deliberately did NOT add it myself: that file is release-gate substrate and Slice 40's territory, and a concurrent leg could be in it. ALSO WORTH AN HITL LOOK: seq-198's stated premise is wrong, so the ruling deserves re-confirmation on its true basis (mechanically-checkable vs opaque-taxonomy) rather than on 'cargo validates one and not the other'.
